gauge.name: Turkey Creek (trib. to Republican River) below Edison

impacts.statement: Water inundates the house immediately southeast of the gage site.  Water covers Highway 136 and also reaches the railroad bridge and tracks just north of the gage site. Widespread lowland and field flooding occurs.

Water reaches Highway 136 at the gage site and also reaches the bottom of the railroad bridge just north of the gage site. In addition, Road 432 will have over 8 feet of water rushing across it just north of Highway 6.
Water reaches the bottom of the Highway 136 bridge at the gage site. Flood water will also start flowing into the bottom of the river gage instrument house.
Water reaches the foundation of the house immediately southeast of the gage site. Road 432 will be flooded in several locations both north and south of Highway 6.
Turkey Creek will begin to flood across Road 432 just north of Highway 6...approximately 2.6 miles upstream of gage site.

value.label: North American Vertical Datum of 1988
value.description: A fixed reference for elevations determined by geodetic leveling. The datum was derived from a general adjustment of the first-order terrestrial leveling nets of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. In the adjustment, only the height of the primary tidal bench mark, referenced to the International Great Lakes Datum of 1985 (IGLD 85) local mean sea level height value, at Father Point, Rimouski, Quebec, Canada was held fixed, thus providing minimum constraint. NAVD 88 and IGLD 85 are identical. However, NAVD 88 bench mark values are given in Helmert orthometric height units while IGLD 85 values are in dynamic heights. See International Great Lakes Datum of 1985, National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929, and geopotential difference. NAVD 88 should not be used as Mean Sea Level.
